list: The official 55 trophies, as listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles before this bounty opened (the two agree on every name, description and grade).
note: Names and descriptions are the official ones, shown as PlayStation publishes them. Every guide below is written for this entry, in our own words, from the official description; where a place or step is not pinned down by the description we say so plainly instead of inventing it.

trophies.guide: The platinum pops on its own the moment the other 54 trophies are earned — there is no separate task behind it. Work through this guide's roadmap in order (story first, then side strands, collectibles, activities and the money goals) and it will unlock at the end of the cleanup stage, usually right after the final 100% completion or the last collectible. Nothing about it can be missed: as long as every other trophy is done, this one follows.

trophies.guide: This is the game's opening mission, Gone Fishing, and it is unmissable: play the story from the start and the trophy unlocks when the mission's closing scene plays. There is nothing to prepare and no side objective to worry about — just follow the on-screen prompts through the mission. If you are past the opening, you already have it.

trophies.guide: Reach 100% on the game's completion checklist. This is the long grind behind the platinum: it counts the story, the side strands, the collectibles and the activities together, so it is normally the last gold before the platinum itself. Track it in the game's own stats screen and use this guide's checklist to clear each family of tasks in turn — story, strangers and contacts, collectibles, then the activity counts. Nothing in it is missable; everything it counts can be finished in free roam after the story.

Check the in-game completion percentage; it pops at 100%.

trophies.guide: Pull off 250 stunts across your playthrough. A stunt is any show-off driving move the game registers — jumps, near misses, long airtime and the like — and the count builds up passively while you drive between missions, so most players will be well on the way by the end of the story. To finish it off, drive fast and loose on open roads: take jumps, thread traffic and use ramps, and watch the counter climb. The official description gives the target of 250; the exact moves that count are the game's own stunt register, which we have not verified in play.

trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try each of the game's 9 activity types at least once. The activities are the side pastimes scattered across Leonida — fishing, the shooting range, drone races, arcade games, bowling, racing and the rest — and one try at each is enough; you do not need to win or finish any of them. The quickest way is to sample one of each as you meet them during the story, ticking them off in this guide's checklist as you go, rather than hunting them all down at the end.

trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Earn a gold medal in all 42 Shooting Range challenges. This is the skill test of the set: each challenge has a score or time threshold for gold, and you need gold on every one of the 42, not just a pass. Work through them weapon by weapon, learn each challenge's target pattern, and replay the ones you miss — there is no limit on retries and nothing here is missable. Leave it for the cleanup stage, when you can focus on it without story missions pulling you away.
trophies.name: The Shootist

trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at all 14 of its locations. Each location hosts its own drone race, and you need a win at every one — a win at one location does not carry over to another. Fly the course cleanly, learn each track's corners, and retry any location you lose; races can be replayed as often as you like. Work through the locations one by one and tick them off in the checklist as each win lands.

trophies.guide: Win 20 different races. The key word is different: winning the same race twice counts once, so you need 20 distinct race events across Leonida. Enter races as you find them, pick a fast car you are comfortable with, and keep a note of which ones you have already won — this guide's checklist is the place to do it. Races are repeatable and never missable, so this is pure cleanup.

trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge. Cal is the fishing rival you meet through the game's fishing activity: take on his challenge and out-fish him. Fishing challenges are about landing the better catch, so use the best rod and bait you have and take your time with the reel. If you lose, challenge him again — the trophy only needs one win, and the challenge is repeatable.

trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at all 18 meditation spots across Leonida. The spots are scenic places around the map where the game lets you sit and meditate; you need to use every one of them. Explore the map's quiet corners — beaches, hilltops, parks and lookouts are the natural candidates — and use the meditate prompt at each spot. Tick each one off as you find it; the trophy pops at 18 of 18. The official description gives the count; the exact spot locations are not pinned down by it, so this is a slow exploration task rather than a checklist you can rush.

The official description names Bret and a unique animal but no location, so this is one to do when his strand offers it rather than hunting blind.

Just keep playing: try new things, take on the activities, and the challenges will fall one by one. The official description gives the target of 50; the full challenge list is the game's own, which we have not verified in play.

trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: With your partner beside you, build up a 4-star wanted level and then lose it and escape. The partner is the key part: this only counts while you are out with your partner, so do it during a stretch of the story when partner outings are available — do not leave it until after the finale. Get the police to 4 stars, then break line of sight, hide until the stars clear, and drive away clean. If the wanted level drops to 3 stars first, build it back up and try again.
trophies.name: Hot Together

trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: With your partner, rob 3 shops in a row without losing your wanted level — the trick is the opposite of the usual escape: you must keep the heat the whole way through all three robberies. Plan a route past three shops close together, hit them one after another with your partner, and keep moving between them so the wanted level never clears. Like Hot Together, this needs your partner beside you, so do it while partner outings are available in the story, not after the finale.

trophies.guide: Discover 100 different vehicles. Every new vehicle you get into counts toward the total, so the fastest way is variety: drive everything you see — cars, bikes, trucks, boats and anything else with wheels — instead of sticking to one favourite. The count builds up naturally across the story and the exploration stages; if you are short at the end, sweep car parks and busy streets for models you have never driven.

trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Take down 5 enemies during a single use of Combat Focus. Combat Focus is the game's slow-down aiming mode: trigger it in a fight with at least 5 enemies in front of you, and drop all 5 before the effect ends. Pick a crowded firefight — a gang shootout or a police standoff — rather than a quiet one-on-one, keep your aim steady, and make every shot count. If the effect ends early, reload the fight and try again.
trophies.name: Gunslinger

trophies.guide: Make an unscheduled departure from VCIA — the Vice City International Airport. In plain terms: get a plane (or another aircraft) off the ground at the airport without going through the normal channels. The official description is deliberately playful and does not spell out the exact method, so treat this as an airport stunt: reach the runways, take an aircraft, and leave by air. Do it while the airport is open to you in the story, and be ready for a wanted level on the way out.

trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store without being detected. Stealth is the whole requirement: get in, take the goods and get out before anyone spots you. Go in quiet, move slowly, avoid the staff's line of sight and the cameras, and do not raise an alarm. If you are spotted, leave and try again — the trophy needs one clean run, and the store can be retried.

trophies.guide: Rob 5 bank vaults and escape from each one. Bank vaults are the big heists of the free-roam world: break into the vault, take the cash and get clear of the police afterwards. You need five separate vault jobs, and each one only counts if you escape — getting caught after the robbery does not count. Plan your getaway before you go in, use a fast car, and work through the vaults one at a time.
trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal

trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob an armored truck and escape. Armored trucks drive set routes around Leonida: intercept one, stop it, break it open and take the cash, then lose the police. A well-placed ram or a roadblock works to stop the truck; once it is open, grab the money fast and get clear before the wanted level climbs. One successful robbery and escape is all it takes.

trophies.guide: Explore all 52 areas of Leonida. The map is divided into named areas, and you need to have visited every one of them — the game tracks which areas you have set foot in. Drive the whole map methodically: cover the cities, the coast, the swamps and the countryside, and check the in-game map for areas you have never entered. It pairs naturally with the collectible sweeps, so do it alongside the cards, meditation spots and WAiNK locations.

trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob an illegal operation belonging to each of the 9 gangs. Gangs run illegal operations around Leonida — drug labs, chop shops, smuggling spots and the like — and you need to hit one operation for every gang, all 9 of them. Learn which gang holds which turf, raid one operation per gang, and keep a per-gang count here so you know which ones are still untouched.

trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach. Head to a bar or beach spot on Ocean Beach with a view of the water, order a cocktail and take it in. It is a quiet moment trophy — no chase, no fight — just the right place at the right time. Any beachfront bar on Ocean Beach should do; sit, order, and let the scene play.

trophies.guide: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style. Pick a vehicle showroom, get into a car inside it, and drive straight out through the glass — the big, loud, classic GTA exit. Expect alarms and a wanted level, so have a getaway plan for the street outside. One dramatic exit is all it takes.

Find the alley, start a game and play it out; the trophy pops when the game is done.

trophies.guide: The description is deliberately vague — 'a partnership with mass appeal' — and the trophy is tied to a partnership moment in the story, most likely a scene where you and your partner do something that draws a crowd. Play the story and watch for a set-piece moment with your partner that plays to an audience; when it happens, the trophy should pop. We have not verified the exact trigger in play, and this guide does not invent one — treat it as a story moment to watch for, and do it before the finale in case it is one-time.

trophies.guide: Make choices — for better or worse. The game tracks the decisions you make, and PSN tracks a count toward 500 for this trophy, so it is about the accumulation of choices across the story and the side content, not a single decision. Keep playing, take the dialogue and story choices as they come, and the count will climb. Some choices may be one-time, so do not skip through decision scenes without thinking — pick a side and live with it.

trophies.guide: Second time's the charm: succeed at something on your second try. The description is a riddle, and the exact event is not pinned down by the official list — the natural reading is a task you fail once and then complete on the retry. If you fail a mission, a challenge or an activity, do not reload an old save: retry it straight away and finish it on the second attempt. Keep this in mind early, before you have burned your first failures on retries that do not count.

trophies.guide: Witness something strange. The description — 'What the hell just happened?' — points at one of the game's odd, scripted events: a UFO, a cryptid, a bizarre encounter out in the wilds of Leonida. Explore the map's strange corners, especially at night or in remote places, and keep your eyes open. The exact event is not pinned down by the official list, so this is a trophy to stumble into while exploring rather than one to force — and it may be one-time, so let the scene play when you find it.

trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Knock someone over with a melee drive-by: hit a person with a melee weapon while driving past. The trick is the combination — you need to be in a moving vehicle and swinging a melee weapon at the same time. Find a quiet stretch of road with a pedestrian, drive slowly past, and swing as you pass. It takes one clean hit, and a slow drive-by is far easier to land than a fast one.

trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Earn $250,000 by laundering Marked Bills through your contacts. Marked Bills are the dirty cash you pick up from heists and robberies: take them to a contact who launders them, and the clean money counts toward the $250,000 target. Keep robbing — vaults, trucks and shops all feed the pile — and launder the bills as you go rather than letting them sit. The official description gives the target; the contacts who launder are the game's own, which we have not verified in play.

trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops. Every dollar you spend in any shop counts — clothes, weapons, food, car mods, anything — and the total is cumulative across the whole playthrough. You will be well on the way by the end of the story just from gearing up; if you are short at the end, buy expensive items you actually want (weapons, outfits, car upgrades) rather than throwing money away. The count is total spending, not one purchase.

They are scattered across the map, so this is another exploration purchase — sweep the cities and the countryside for sale signs, and buy each garage as you find it. The official description gives the target of 8; the garage locations are the game's own, which we have not verified in play.
